answer: A key earns credit only by hitting a surprise attendance window, shown 4 seconds early and shut at a horizon of 70 seconds. In that span it signs a nonce issued at its registry vertex. A late or reused signature, or one aimed at another vertex, slashes a 140-unit reef deposit. Short hidden windows collide if one process covers many keys, so each alias needs a live signer. An honest key locks 140 units and one signer. A farm of 1,000 aliases must run 1,000 signers and lock 140,000 units, since reef deposits never merge. Extra machines still work; they cannot share a vertex.
